conventions.convention: Full AC is assumed throughout; it supplies injective resolutions, products of sectionwise lifts, and refinement choices.
Čech cohomology of the space is the filtered colimit over open covers, using ordered alternating cochains; derived cohomology means ordinary right-derived global sections, without compact supports.
Cover order at most m+1 means each point belongs to at most m+1 distinct cover members; local finiteness means a neighborhood meets only finitely many members.

The partial free resolution has indices 0 through ℓ with ℓ=2N+1; it is exact at the module and all free terms except possibly the leftmost. The same chosen W works for every nonempty coordinate subpolydisc D and every positive cohomological degree.
In the point example, W is chosen for the particular quotient module. In the hyperplane example, D is any coordinate polydisc containing 0, and its coordinate discs need not be centered at 0.

load_bearing.statement: Assume full AC. For a metric space X and an abelian sheaf F on its metric topology, the canonical comparison from refinement-limit Čech cohomology to derived sheaf cohomology is a natural isomorphism in every integer degree q≥0, agreeing with the global-sections identification in degree zero.
Assume full AC. Every open cover of a nonempty Euclidean open subset Ω of R^m, m≥1, has a locally finite open refinement such that every point belongs to at most m+1 members.
Assume full AC. For every nonempty open Ω⊆R^m with m≥1 and every sheaf G of abelian groups on Ω, ordinary derived-functor sheaf cohomology H^q(Ω,G) vanishes for every integer q>m.

Assume full AC. For N≥0 and a coherent analytic module F on an open neighborhood of x∈C^N, there is a coordinate polydisc W centered at x such that H^q(D,F|D)=0 for every nonempty coordinate polydisc D⊆W and every integer q>0. Scalar sheaf cohomology on each D is computed by its global smooth Dolbeault complex and vanishes in positive degrees. W may be chosen subordinate to a partial finite-rank free resolution indexed through ℓ=2N+1, exact except possibly at the leftmost free term.

concerns.concern: The title, “Locally finite refinements of Euclidean open covers have order at most the dimension plus one,” reads as a universal bound on locally finite refinements. The Statement correctly proves existence of a refinement with that bound. Arbitrary locally finite refinements can have higher multiplicity: in R, three distinct overlapping intervals refining the one-member cover {R}, together with R itself, form a finite open cover with multiplicity four at a common point. The title should express existence.

seams_checked.note: Read the coherent-module definition and Oka supplier, including its matrix-kernel, bounded-degree-relation, and coherent-calculus arguments. The local theorem uses the stated finite partial resolution and closure under kernels. It does not assume leftmost exactness or a global free resolution.

Both examples use coherence of finite free analytic modules and closure under cokernels. Their quotient identifications are proved locally by stalks. The point example chooses W for its particular quotient; the hyperplane example proves its stronger arbitrary-polydisc vanishing separately using scalar acyclicity.

Read the section-topology lemma, pseudoconvex-intersection lemma, and compact-projective finiteness theorem. Local vanishing is applied after shrinking inside the relevant coherent-kernel neighborhoods. The intersection lemma uses the ordinary Euclidean cohomological-dimension bound on chart-open components, rather than claiming that arbitrary chart intersections are coordinate polydiscs.
